cohort: The study included 36 postpartum women, divided into two groups of 18 each: one group who underwent cesarean delivery and another who underwent vaginal delivery.
finding: Postpartum women who underwent cesarean delivery experienced significantly higher nonspecific low back pain intensities and weaker transversus abdominis strength than those who underwent vaginal delivery, though NSLBP intensity showed no significant association with TrA or LM strength in either group.
mod_finding: Women undergoing cesarean delivery experienced significantly higher nonspecific low back pain intensities and weaker transversus abdominis strength compared to those undergoing vaginal delivery, while lumbar multifidus strength remained similar between the groups.
